canonical_decision.principle: Scenekunst-Badge points document learning and field participation. They do not by themselves prove an employment contract, project engagement, artistic appointment or institutional leadership mandate.

legacy_career_id_migration.reason: Canonical Badge id and job rebuilding use `scenekunst`; the legacy `teater` career id was disconnected from the Badge progression. Runtime title resolution keeps a narrow legacy alias for existing position state.

legacy_cross_requirement.reason: The legacy rule would gate the third Badge tier (Produksjonsassistent), not a meaningful senior artistic threshold, and had never been active for the canonical `scenekunst` Badge id. It is not carried into the canonical contract.

salary_mapping.interpretation: Civication game economy only; not a claim about Norwegian market wages.

evidence_notes.claim: Skuespiller is a real occupation, but work can be institutional, company-based or project/freelance. Badge identity therefore cannot equal a fixed-salary employment contract.
Dramaturg is a real professional function and may be institutionally employed or work freelance/project-based.
Directors commonly work freelance/project-based, including theatre directors; some are employed or operate companies.
Choreographers often work on own projects and many are self-employed.
Scenetechnical work is a concrete professional field; technical competence must not be inferred from Badge points alone.
Teatersjef is registered as a leadership occupation/title, supporting an appointment gate rather than automatic progression employment.
Norwegian scenekunst institutions distinguish employees from freelancers and operate with employment/tariff frameworks for stage professions.
